lead: New York City's apartment buildings, brownstones and oil-heated buildings make its fire damage unlike anywhere else. SootMend helps homes and businesses in all five boroughs recover from fire, smoke and soot.
risk: apartment fires that spread smoke to many units, lithium-ion battery fires, and oil burner puff-backs
why: Two in three New Yorkers rent, and most live in multi-unit buildings. A fire in one apartment sends smoke up stairwells, elevator shafts and halls to units many floors away, and water from fire hoses runs down to the floors below. Lithium-ion batteries in e-bikes and scooters have become a leading cause of serious fires in the city in recent years.

More than one in ten city homes still heat with fuel oil, often from a building boiler, so puff-backs can coat apartments in oily soot. Nearly four in ten homes were built before 1940. Brownstones, row houses and walk-ups often have old wiring and shared walls.
problems: Smoke in apartments far from the fire
Water damage on floors below a fire
tips: Charge e-bikes and scooters only with the maker's charger, away from exits, and never overnight.
Close the door behind you when you leave a burning apartment.
Keep hallways and fire escapes clear.
Ask your building about its boiler service schedule.
insurance: Co-op and condo owners need their own policy for interiors and belongings, because the building's policy rarely covers everything inside a unit.
areas: SootMend works in all five boroughs, including the Upper West Side, Harlem, Park Slope, Williamsburg, Astoria, Riverdale, the Rockaways and Staten Island's North Shore.

faq.q: Who pays for smoke damage in my New York apartment from a fire on another floor?
faq.a: The building's policy covers common areas and the structure. Your renters, co-op or condo policy covers your belongings and extra living costs. Report the damage to your landlord or board and your insurer.
